title: DOISST v2.1 shows one third of its 7 July 2020 satellite-input step near drifting buoys (0.02 against 0.06 C, 60S-60N), so buoy checks underestimate it; the 2005 step is reduced less
abstract: Question: NOAA Daily OISST v2.1 (DOISST) has a warm step of about 0.07 C on 7 July 2020, caused by a change of the Navy MetOp-A AVHRR input from L2P v1.0 to v2.0. Buoy checks show a much smaller step. Where does DOISST keep the step, and how much can buoy validation see? Approach: we measured the step of DOISST minus ERA5 in bins of distance from the nearest in situ observation of the same day (iQuam drifting buoys, moorings, Argo floats, ships), with 30-day windows and control years, and repeated the test for the 1 January 2005 step. We added a lag test, a placebo date, the local analysis gain toward in situ data, and an independent test of the NAVO input offset against drifters. Results: in cells with a drifting buoy on the same day, the 2020 step is +0.020 C (95% interval 0.013 to 0.029); it is +0.039 C at 50-100 km, +0.057 C at 100-200 km and +0.062 to +0.066 C at 200-800 km. The area-weighted step is +0.059 C, so drifter cells show 34% of it; 66% of the ocean is more than 200 km from a same-day drifter. Ship cells show the full step (+0.071 C). The 2005 step is +0.072 C at drifter cells and +0.125 C at 200-800 km (ratio 0.58). A placebo date gives near zero in all bins. The same-day gain toward drifters stays at about 0.13-0.18 from 1984 to 2021 (ships 0.02-0.035), and on 2-degree boxes the step does not depend on drifter density, so the reduction is local. NAVO MetOp-A minus drifters changes by +0.096 C (0.055 to 0.137) relative to 2019, and v2.0 keeps 1.43 times more pixels. Conclusion: validation against assimilated drifters sees about one third of a satellite-input step; drifter and mooring estimates of 0.03-0.04 C for 2020 are 2-3 times too small. Limitation: ERA5 is the reference and must have no step at these dates; distance bins also sample different regions; DOISST internal data are not public.

citations.reason: Found the 7 July 2020 step; we reuse its daily DOISST-minus-CCI series (figure 1) and explain why its buoy estimate is small.
Found the NAVO v1.0 to v2.0 cause; our independent input-offset test agrees, and our distance test explains its small DOISST-minus-drifter change.
